What's new

What changed, release by release.

Every change to VertexForm that you can see or hear, newest first. It's the project's changelog, so nothing here is planned work: all of it is live.

2.4.03 November 2026

Privacy page

  • A page that says what happens to your camera and your data, in plain words: what's kept in this browser and for how long, what your browser downloads and from where, and how to export or erase everything. The tests check the code keeps its promises: no cookies, no analytics, no uploads.

Finding your way around

  • The footer is a small sitemap: the trainer, the library, the skill paths, how it works, the Form Lab, questions, What's new and privacy.
  • The homepage's exercise list is now a row of small drawings, one per exercise, each opening its page in the library.
  • A missing page says so and offers the homepage, the library and the trainer.
  • Menu links on the homepage stop with the section right under the header, instead of a little way down.

Sharing

  • Links to VertexForm show a preview card with its name and what it does.

Easier to read

  • Hint text is brighter, so it's readable on every background.
  • Pages no longer jump as their fonts load, and nothing scrolls sideways on a phone.
2.3.02 November 2026

Eight more exercises

  • Bulgarian split squat: the front knee and an upright torso, counted only with the back foot up on a bench.
  • Pistol squat: depth on the standing leg, and the free leg has to stay off the floor.
  • Dips: elbows to about 90° on parallel bars.
  • Australian row: chest to a low bar with the body in one straight line.
  • Negative pull-up: graded on how slowly you lower, 3 seconds or more.
  • Pull-up: from a dead hang until the chin clears the bar.
  • L-sit: legs straight and level with the hips, held for time.
  • V-sit: feet raised well above the hips, held for time.
  • Each has its own coaching lines and spoken name in all three voices, so all eighteen exercises can go in a workout.

Skill paths

  • The Legs and Core paths are now tracked from start to finish, and the Pull path up to ten pull-ups.
  • The trainer's menu shows your nearest unlocks: the two skills your saved sets are closest to, what's left in words, and a button to train it.
  • Workouts can plan your next unlocks: one step for each of the skills you're closest to, at its goal amount, so finishing the workout can unlock them.

Exercise library

  • A new page with every exercise: what it scores, what a good rep looks like, the mistakes it flags in the coach's own words, and the skills it unlocks. Each one links straight to its setup in the trainer.

What's new

  • This page: every change you can see or hear, newest first.

A quieter design

  • Lighter headings, solid buttons and ruled figure plates, after comparing the site with Linear, Raycast and Apple. The grade colours now only mean scores.
  • Removed effects that made the site look generated: the light following the pointer, click sparks, magnetic buttons, tilting cards and decoding text.
  • Nothing flashes while the homepage loads, and screens in the trainer grow out of the button you pressed.
2.2.028 October 2026

Exercises and coaching

  • Pike push-up, side plank, hollow hold, mountain climbers and dead hang.
  • Every exercise says its own setup line when you're out of position.
  • Rep replay: watch each rep back beside the ideal form and save the ones you want.
  • Daily challenges for 7, 14 or 30 days.

Skill paths

  • 32 skills in five paths (Push, Pull, Legs, Core, Conditioning), drawn as trees that grow and bloom. Tracked skills unlock from your real saved sets, and each skill shows your best try against its goal.

The website

  • A 3D hero that grades a simulated rep with the real engine, a pinned "How it works" story, exercise popups that turn the drawing into a 3D model, and the Form Lab, where sliders drive the real scoring.
  • The homepage speaks in the trainer's recorded voice.

The trainer

  • The exercise picker is an instrument: the exercise you point at does its rep live.
  • Results land with a grade dial, a rep chart that draws itself and fault dots for every rep they were flagged in.
